[CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.14395) combines next-item recommendation loss with weighted InfoNCE between two randomly cropped, masked or reordered histories, using other sequences as negatives. [CoSeRec](https://arxiv.org/html/2108.06479) retains recommendation plus symmetric NT-Xent, adding correlated-item substitution/insertion and length-dependent augmentation selection. Its documented controls include leave-one-operator-out, all operator pairs, short-sequence augmentation sets and corruption-strength sweeps. Removing crop/reorder improves Beauty results; removing insertion/substitution hurts both studied datasets. Excessive corruption or contrastive weight degrades performance. [DuoRec](https://arxiv.org/html/2110.05730) uses recommendation cross-entropy plus contrastive regularization pairing dropout-generated representations with representations of histories sharing the training target. Ablations compare random augmentation, dropout-only UCL, target-based SCL and UCL+SCL; simply adding the latter two losses underperforms DuoRec’s pairing.

False invariance is a documented concern: deleting/masking predictive interactions or disrupting order can change intent while the objective forces agreement; other users can also become false negatives. [EC4SRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.01347) already uses explanation-guided item importance to construct positive/negative views, so targeted history editing alone is established territory. Semantic isolation need not imply irrelevance: an isolated interaction may indicate a new interest; this is an inference requiring validation.

The three named methods do not establish detached clean-to-augmented output KL as their loss. A proposed formulation is L_rec + λT² KL(stopgrad[p_clean,T] || p_deleted,T), on identical candidate support; this distinction does not establish novelty. Necessary proposed controls: matched-count random deletion, matched-recency deletion, reversed targeting, no consistency loss, dropout-only consistency, symmetric/non-detached KL and InfoNCE under the same deletion policy. Report deletion-rate and history-length sensitivity using the pinned macro validation HR@10.
